The lessons will be marked as incomplete. Your gestures and the Do not show again setting will stay the same.
Would you like to practice first?

Learn the remote gestures with a simulated computer. You do not need to connect. You choose when to move to the next exercise. You can also connect now. If you choose Do not show again, you can still open the lessons from this screen.

Practice with a simulated computer on this phone. Nothing is sent to a real computer. Start with the first lesson, choose another, or try free practice. Passed exercises are saved. You choose when to continue.
You completed all the lessons. You can repeat them, use free practice, or return to the connection screen.

Explore a simulated computer. Open Start or Run, type in the editor, and switch between the editor, Documents and the browser. Use the same gestures as the real remote. This practice uses basic braille letters; when connected, NVDA uses its own braille table. Open the practice menu to choose more keys.
5. Hold a key to switch windows
Back always lets you ask to exit. From that screen you can also open the practice menu. Leaving requires confirmation.

Locate the points using your usual braille layout. In control mode, send the letter A. With the default gestures, this is a short press on point 1. These are your current controls:\n%1$s
Open the menu. It lets you choose commands and get help during practice. Then choose Keep practicing to return.\n%1$s
Ask to exit, then choose Keep practicing. This lets you check how to leave before learning more gestures.\n%1$s
Send Tab to move to the next control in the simulated editor.\n%1$s
Send Shift+Tab to move to the previous control.\n%1$s
Send Right arrow to move the cursor.\n%1$s
Send Enter to open the selected item.\n%1$s
Send Escape to close a simulated menu or dialog.\n%1$s
Send Control+A to select the editor text. A prepared modifier applies to the next key. Doing its gesture again cancels it.\n%1$s
Send Control+C to copy the sample text. This practice has its own clipboard.\n%1$s
Send Control+V to paste the sample text.\n%1$s
Send the Windows key to open the simulated Start menu.\n%1$s
Send Windows+R to open Run. You can prepare Windows from the menu and then type R in control mode.\n%1$s
Hold Alt, send Tab at least twice, then release Alt to choose a window. The phone will name each window.\n%1$s
Change to keyboard mode. In this mode, braille cells are sent to the computer for writing.\n%1$s
Write a braille A in keyboard mode. This practice uses basic letters. On a real connection, the input table selected in NVDA determines the text.\n%1$s
Write a space to finish the word.\n%1$s
Erase the last character or braille cell.\n%1$s
Finish the braille input and send Enter.\n%1$s
Return to control mode to use letters as computer keys and combine them with modifiers.\n%1$s
Mute the remote voice on this phone. CAN Talk will still read its own controls.\n%1$s
The simulated remote voice is muted. Unmute it to hear new messages.\n%1$s
Your progress is saved. You can resume later.
